extracted.intended_audience: QHP issuers, State Exchange officials (FFEs and SBE-FPs), State regulators, legal and policy stakeholders submitting comments
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed Federal rule amendments and associated guidance for evaluating/certifying non-network plans, conducting ECP reviews, auditing issuer compliance (APTC/CSR/user fees), calculating CMPs, administrative appeals, and QHP Quality Improvement Strategies (QIS). Intended for entities subject to Exchange regulation and parties commenting on the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: State legal authority and technical capacity for ECP certification reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider factors related to a State's legal authority, State ECP requirements compared to ECP requirements under § 156.235 and proposed § 156.236, definition of an ECP, process for identifying qualified ECPs, data collection systems and methodologies to collect and review ECP data, delegation of ECP review to other entities, compliance and enforcement mechanisms, and consumer assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS will consider all these criteria when determining if an FFE State has sufficient authority and the technical capacity to conduct ECP certification reviews including for non-network plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Federal ECP List or State process to identify ECPs accepting benefit amounts in full
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the FFE State utilizes the Federal ECP List or has a process they use to identify qualified ECPs that may accept a non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full (proposed § 155.1051(e)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential to identify the exact geographic location and distribution of ECPs available within an issuer's service area that may accept a non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full to ensure issuers include ECPs 'where available' consistent with ACA section 1311(c)(1)(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of issuer data on offers/acceptance of benefit amounts to ECPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the FFE State collects information from issuers regarding the status of offers of benefit amounts as payment in full to an ECP (proposed § 155.1051(e)(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This data is an important metric to assess an issuer's compliance with minimum percentage, category per county, and Indian health care requirements under proposed § 156.236(b)(1)-(b)(3), evaluated based on measurements of benefit amounts offered to or accepted by an ECP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of State/local market and demographic factors in ECP reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: States' unique knowledge on local factors (market conditions, geographic constraints, areas with limited economic resources, provider shortages, workforce issues, and population demographics) should be leveraged in ECP reviews of non-network plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These local factors can strengthen ECP reviews and may justify allowing FFE States flexibility in how they review non-network plans for qualitative information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-network plan submission requirements (proposed § 156.236(b)(4)-(b)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that non-network plans must submit to the FFE, including strategy for conducting outreach to ECPs, making benefit amounts public to enrollees, methodologies for determining benefit amounts, strategy for publishing consumer‑friendly information on balance billing and potential out‑of‑pocket costs, availability of exceptions processes for enrollees unable to locate providers who accept benefit amounts as payment in full, and customer service resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors are specific to non-network plans and reflect additional safeguards to ensure plans maintain access to providers without traditional network arrangements; they are qualitative measures that may require different data collection methods than quantitative metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish qualitative vs quantitative measures in non-network plan review
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that information described under § 156.236(b)(4)-(b)(9) are qualitative measures and would likely require different data collection methods compared to the more quantitative measures (minimum percentage, category per county, Indian health care requirements) under § 156.236(b)(1)-(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS opted to defer to FFE States on how they wish to review non-network plans for qualitative information, but seeks comment on whether HHS should better align reviews across the FFE by enumerating these factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of existing certification provisions to non-network plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to §§ 155.1050 (including its heading), 156.275, and 156.810 to clarify that provisions within these sections apply to certification of non-network plans in the same manner as they apply to network plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures regulatory consistency so non-network plans are subject to the same relevant procedural certification provisions as network plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of HHS audits/compliance reviews for APTC, CSR, and user fee programs (proposed § 156.480(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS or its designee may audit or conduct a compliance review to assess compliance with all requirements related to APTC, CSR, and user fee programs applicable to issuers offering a QHP through an Exchange, not limited to 45 CFR part 156 subpart E and § 156.50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, HHS may assess compliance with premium payment/grace period requirements at § 156.270(g) and other enrollment/payment requirements outside subpart E that affect proper APTC administration; compliance reviews follow standards in § 156.715.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of compliance reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS may conduct compliance reviews as needed, including on an annual basis, rather than only on an ad hoc basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual compliance reviews can allow issuers to proactively correct data inaccuracies prior to audits and more quickly resolve APTC over‑ or underpayments; HHS is not proposing regulatory text amendments here but clarifying preamble policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors and lawful purpose(s) considered when determining CMP amounts (proposed § 156.805(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the amount of CMPs, HHS would consider the factors listed in § 156.805(b)(1)-(3) and also identify the lawful purpose or purposes of the CMP amount (e.g., penalize, bring into compliance, or make a wronged party whole). Statutory limits and considerations such as previous record of compliance and gravity of the violation also apply (see PHS Act § 2723(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS will increase transparency by identifying the lawful purpose(s) underpinning a CMP amount; statutory cap example: $100 per day per individual (adjusted), and HHS may weigh past compliance records and severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to impose CMPs against issuers in State Exchanges and SBE‑FPs (proposed § 156.805(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a State notifies HHS it is not enforcing applicable requirements or HHS determines a State is failing to substantially enforce them, HHS may impose CMPs against issuers in State Exchanges or SBE‑FPs for violations of any Exchange requirements and standards applicable to issuers offering a QHP, not limited to subpart E or § 156.50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amendment aligns with HHS statutory authority and does not supplant State enforcement; the process still requires State notice or HHS determination following the standards in § 150.201 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ subpoena authority in administrative appeals (proposed § 156.903)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow an administrative law judge presiding over an administrative appeal of a QHP issuer sanction to issue subpoenas, on the ALJ's own motion or at a party's request, if subpoenas are reasonably necessary for the full presentation of a case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal includes procedural requirements: a party must file a written request at least 5 calendar days before the hearing, identify witness(es)/documents and their addresses/locations with sufficient particularity, specify the pertinent facts expected to be established, and indicate why those facts cannot be established without a subpoena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of discovery for CMP appeals resulting from audits (proposed § 156.935 amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery provisions would not apply to administrative appeals of proposed CMPs for violations identified through audits of APTC, CSR, or user fee programs conducted per § 156.480(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: audit processes (entrance/exit conferences, collaborative audits, opportunities to refute findings, and § 156.806 notice/response process) provide issuers and HHS with the relevant information and reduce the need for duplicative, time‑consuming discovery in appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Improvement Strategy (QIS) submission requirements (§ 156.1130)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require QHP issuers to submit QISs addressing any two of the five topic areas listed in section 1311(g)(1) of the ACA (improving health outcomes, preventing readmissions, improving patient safety/reducing medical errors, promoting wellness/health, reducing health and healthcare disparities), without mandating specific topic areas, beginning PY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers participating in an Exchange for two or more consecutive years must implement and report on a QIS for each QHP; issuers may select quality measures (e.g., Marketplace Quality Rating System) or other performance targets and tie increased reimbursement/market‑based incentives to performance; the change provides flexibility for issuers to select topics most relevant to their population.
